categories.Fire: Active fire, smoke, burning, or electrical sparks that could start a fire.
categories.Medical Emergency: Injury, fainting, seizure, severe illness, or anyone needing urgent care.
categories.Theft/Break-in: Stolen items, forced entry, or suspicious people trying to enter.
categories.Harassment/Assault: Physical fights, threats, sexual harassment, or bullying.
categories.Infrastructure Fault: Something visibly broken: burst pipes, broken doors, cracked walls, faulty wiring, blocked toilets, damaged equipment.
categories.Road Accident: Vehicle crashes or people hit by vehicles on or near campus.
categories.Service Outage: Power, water, or Wi-Fi/internet not working or badly degraded in an area, with nothing visibly broken.
categories.Other/Non-urgent: Noise complaints, lost items, general queries, or anything that fits no other category.

severity.High: Danger to life or safety right now, or something actively getting worse. Respond immediately.
severity.Medium: Real damage, loss, or disruption, but nobody is in immediate danger. Respond the same day.
severity.Low: Minor, routine, or can wait. Includes incidents already resolved with no injuries.

severity_rules: Label the worst credible reading of the report.
Category does not decide severity; read the details in the text.
Whole-complex or exam-time outages are Medium.
Theft in progress is High; theft already discovered is Medium.
Already resolved incidents with no injuries are Low.

entities.LOCATION: Any place from the gazetteer: facilities, complexes, and rooms. Example: library, P complex, A1.2, boom gate.
entities.DATE_TIME: When it happened or is happening. Example: last night, at 3pm, since morning, now.
entities.ASSET: A physical object or equipment involved. Example: laptop, router, pipe, generator, transformer.
entities.PERSON_ROLE: Who is involved, by role only, never by name. Example: student, lecturer, security guard, cleaner.

entity_rules: Tag the smallest span that identifies the thing (P complex, not the whole of P complex).
Rooms and complexes are separate LOCATION spans.
Tag only what is stated; do not guess missing times or places.
Vague words like everywhere or outside are not LOCATION unless they name a gazetteer place.

language.English: Written entirely in English. Local slang or abbreviations still count as English.
language.Mixed: Contains both English and Shona words or phrases, in the same sentence or the same report.
language.Shona: Written entirely in Shona. Common loanwords and place names do not count against it.

language_rules: Judge the whole report, not a single word.
Facility and complex names (library, boom gate, P complex) never decide the language.
A Shona sentence with one common English loanword is still Shona.
A real switch of phrases or clauses between the two languages is Mixed.
